answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 20 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The umber multiplier is published, charged in zephyr, and saffron lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4454 identities would post 2042 proofs and burn roughly 59 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
